title: Cool koalas
paragraphs: When you think of a cute, furry wild animal, you often picture a koala. These adorable-looking creatures appear docile and friendly, so it’s no wonder people are concerned about the future of the species after the devastating bushfires that destroyed parts of Australia earlier this year. Luckily, many survived, which gives us a chance to continue to learn more about these marsupials.

Australia’s native and unique wildlife such as kangaroos, platypus and koalas, are under constant threat from human activity and natural disasters. It’s thought at least a billion animals lost their lives as a result of this year’s bushfires. Recently, drones and thermal imaging technology have been used to track their movements to help them keep safe. Protecting these unique species is important because, as The Australian Koala Foundation estimates, there are now possibly as few as 43,000 koalas in the wild.

So, what is so special about koalas and what makes them so ‘cool’? Maybe we envy their ability to sleep for up to 22 hours day! Or could it be their laid-back appearance due to the fact that they are herbivores and mainly feed on juicy eucalyptus leaves, which take a lot of time and energy to digest.

What is amazing is that because they often live in a dry and hot environment, they drink very little water. So, how do they survive? Well, scientists have discovered that these wild mammals lick running water off the smooth surface of a tree trunk when it is raining. This phenomenon is called "stemflow". Valentina Mella, the lead author of the research and an ethnologist from the University of Sydney, told the BBC: "I think the main message is that behavioural observations in the wild are very important to establish what is normal and what is unusual, and to truly understand what animals need. If we watch them carefully, they will tell us."

So, despite the word ‘koala’ meaning 'no drink' or 'no water' in the Aboriginal language, it seems that even these sleepy creatures do need a drink sometimes. And if we’re to encourage them to flourish, we need to conserve their habitat.

vocabulary.entry: docile /ˈdəʊsaɪl/ adj. 温顺的；驯服的
vocabulary.example: The horse is very docile and easy to control.
vocabulary.translation: 这匹马非常温顺，很容易驾驭。

vocabulary.example: The hurricane had a devastating effect on the coastal town.
vocabulary.translation: 这场飓风对这座沿海小镇造成了毁灭性的影响。

vocabulary.translation: 由于风力强劲，丛林大火迅速蔓延。

vocabulary.example: The kangaroo is a well-known marsupial native to Australia.
vocabulary.translation: 袋鼠是澳大利亚本土著名的有袋动物。

vocabulary.entry: native /ˈneɪtɪv/ adj. 本土的；原产的
vocabulary.example: The panda is a native animal of China.
vocabulary.translation: 熊猫是中国的本土动物。

vocabulary.entry: unique /juˈniːk/ adj. 独一无二的；独特的
vocabulary.example: Each person's fingerprints are unique.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的。

vocabulary.entry: constant /ˈkɒnstənt/ adj. 持续的；不断的

vocabulary.translation: 这个婴儿需要父母时刻的照料。

vocabulary.translation: 这位农民用无人机监测农作物的生长情况。

vocabulary.entry: thermal imaging /ˈθɜːml ˈɪmɪdʒɪŋ/ n. 热成像
vocabulary.example: Thermal imaging can detect heat sources in the dark.
vocabulary.translation: 热成像技术能在黑暗中探测热源。

vocabulary.example: This rare species is protected by the local government.
vocabulary.translation: 这种珍稀物种受到当地政府的保护。

vocabulary.entry: laid-back /ˌleɪd ˈbæk/ adj. 悠然自得的；从容的
vocabulary.example: She has a laid-back attitude towards life.
vocabulary.translation: 她对生活抱着一种悠然自得的态度。

vocabulary.example: The cow is a typical herbivore that feeds on grass.
vocabulary.translation: 牛是典型的食草动物，以草为食。

vocabulary.example: The orange is fresh and juicy.
vocabulary.translation: 这个橙子新鲜又多汁。

vocabulary.entry: eucalyptus leaf /ˌjuːkəˈlɪptəs liːf/ n. 桉树叶
vocabulary.example: Koalas mainly eat eucalyptus leaves for their daily diet.
vocabulary.translation: 考拉的日常饮食主要是桉树叶。

vocabulary.example: It takes time for the body to digest heavy food.
vocabulary.translation: 身体需要时间来消化油腻的食物。

vocabulary.example: Humans, dogs and cats are all mammals.
vocabulary.translation: 人类、狗和猫都是哺乳动物。

vocabulary.translation: 大象用鼻子捡起了香蕉。

vocabulary.example: Stemflow provides water for some animals living in forests.
vocabulary.translation: 茎流为一些生活在森林里的动物提供了水分。

vocabulary.entry: ethnologist /eθˈnɒlədʒɪst/ n. 动物行为学家
vocabulary.example: The ethnologist spent years observing the behaviour of chimpanzees.
vocabulary.translation: 这位动物行为学家花了数年时间观察黑猩猩的行为。

vocabulary.entry: flourish /ˈflʌrɪʃ/ v. 繁衍；茁壮成长
vocabulary.example: Plants flourish in warm and moist soil.
vocabulary.translation: 植物在温暖湿润的土壤里茁壮成长。

vocabulary.example: Destroying forests will threaten the habitat of many animals.
vocabulary.translation: 破坏森林会威胁到许多动物的栖息地。

sentences.english: When you think of a cute, furry wild animal, you often picture a koala.
sentences.chinese: 当你想到一种可爱毛茸茸的野生动物时，脑海里往往会浮现出考拉的样子。

sentences.english: These adorable-looking creatures appear docile and friendly, so it’s no wonder people are concerned about the future of the species after the devastating bushfires that destroyed parts of Australia earlier this year.
sentences.chinese: 这些模样讨人喜欢的动物看起来温顺又友善，所以在今年年初澳大利亚部分地区遭遇毁灭性丛林大火后，人们会担忧这个物种的未来，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.english: Luckily, many survived, which gives us a chance to continue to learn more about these marsupials.
sentences.chinese: 幸运的是，许多考拉幸存了下来，这让我们有机会继续深入了解这些有袋动物。

sentences.english: Australia’s native and unique wildlife such as kangaroos, platypus and koalas, are under constant threat from human activity and natural disasters.
sentences.chinese: 袋鼠、鸭嘴兽、考拉这类澳大利亚本土特有的野生动物，持续面临着人类活动和自然灾害的威胁。

sentences.english: It’s thought at least a billion animals lost their lives as a result of this year’s bushfires.
sentences.chinese: 据悉，今年的丛林大火已导致至少十亿只动物丧生。

sentences.english: Recently, drones and thermal imaging technology have been used to track their movements to help them keep safe.
sentences.chinese: 最近，无人机和热成像技术被用于追踪考拉的行踪，以保障它们的安全。

sentences.english: Protecting these unique species is important because, as The Australian Koala Foundation estimates, there are now possibly as few as 43,000 koalas in the wild.
sentences.chinese: 保护这些独特物种十分重要，因为澳大利亚考拉基金会估计，目前野生考拉的数量可能仅剩下4.3万只。

sentences.english: So, what is so special about koalas and what makes them so ‘cool’?
sentences.chinese: 那么，考拉到底有什么特别之处，又是什么让它们如此“受欢迎”呢？

sentences.english: Maybe we envy their ability to sleep for up to 22 hours day!
sentences.chinese: 或许是我们羡慕它们一天能睡足足22个小时的本事！

sentences.english: Or could it be their laid-back appearance due to the fact that they are herbivores and mainly feed on juicy eucalyptus leaves, which take a lot of time and energy to digest.
sentences.chinese: 又或者是它们那副悠然自得的模样——因为考拉是食草动物，主要以水分充足的桉树叶为食，而消化这些树叶需要耗费大量的时间和精力。

sentences.english: What is amazing is that because they often live in a dry and hot environment, they drink very little water.
sentences.chinese: 令人惊叹的是，由于长期生活在干燥炎热的环境中，考拉的饮水量极少。
那么它们是如何生存的呢？

sentences.english: Well, scientists have discovered that these wild mammals lick running water off the smooth surface of a tree trunk when it is raining.
sentences.chinese: 科学家发现，这种野生哺乳动物会在下雨时，舔食顺着光滑树干流下的雨水。

sentences.english: Valentina Mella, the lead author of the research and an ethnologist from the University of Sydney, told the BBC: "I think the main message is that behavioural observations in the wild are very important to establish what is normal and what is unusual, and to truly understand what animals need.
sentences.chinese: 该研究的第一作者、悉尼大学的动物行为学家瓦伦蒂娜·梅拉在接受BBC采访时表示：“我认为核心启示是，野外行为观察对于判断动物行为的正常与异常、真正了解动物需求至关重要。

sentences.english: If we watch them carefully, they will tell us."
sentences.chinese: 只要我们仔细观察，动物们就会向我们‘诉说’它们的需求。”

sentences.english: So, despite the word ‘koala’ meaning 'no drink' or 'no water' in the Aboriginal language, it seems that even these sleepy creatures do need a drink sometimes.
sentences.chinese: 因此，尽管在澳大利亚原住民的语言中，“考拉”一词意为“不喝水”，但事实证明，即便是这些嗜睡的小家伙，有时也需要补充水分。

sentences.english: And if we’re to encourage them to flourish, we need to conserve their habitat.
sentences.chinese: 而如果我们想要让考拉种群得以繁衍壮大，就必须保护好它们的栖息地。
